messages:
marta: quick summary of the head-to-head I ran this morning (7B open model, pref/dec split) across us-west1 (A100) and eu-west1 (H100). raw runs attached below.

marta: TL;DR — H100 wins latency and throughput, but region pricing flips $/1M depending on kernel. numbers are for steady-state single-request prefill + decode (seq=1024 prefill, decode=256).

jonathan: can you drop the concrete numbers? trying to size Dedicated pools.

marta: sure — exact medians from 2000 samples each: 
- us-west1 A100 (fp16, cuBLAS+custom-kernel): prefill p50=115ms, decode p50=78ms, tokens/sec=580, cost per 1M tokens ~= $2.12
- eu-west1 H100 (fp16, Triton-optim kernel): prefill p50=82ms, decode p50=45ms, tokens/sec=920, cost per 1M tokens ~= $1.55

marta: note: A100 run used batch=1, KV cache warm; H100 had same. network tail noise included.

rahul: interesting — are the cost numbers infra-only or include storage/egress?

marta: infra-only compute + GPU runtime. I used our internal price sheet: A100 base hourly $3.10, H100 $5.20 adjusted by observed token throughput. no egress/storage.

tara.s: any kernel differences called out? which kernel on A100 was the best?

marta: on A100, our tensorkernel variant with fused attention (v3) edged out Triton. for H100, Triton-optimized attention + cuBLAS fallback was best. kernel choices: 
```
A100: tensorkernel-v3 -> fallback cuBLAS
H100: triton-attn-v2 -> cuBLAS-fallback
```

jonathan: perf delta looks big for decode. 45ms vs 78ms is material. how stable are those p95s?

marta: p95s: A100 decode p95=210ms, H100 decode p95=98ms. prefill p95 A100=360ms, H100=150ms. tails on A100 more volatile under burst.

rahul: ok — for Dedicated sizing: using tokens/sec, H100 gives ~1.6x throughput so you need fewer GPUs but cost per GPU higher. break-even depends on utilization. did you compute break-even util?

marta: yep: simple calc w/ our per-GPU price & perf: break-even util ~65%. below that A100 cheaper; above that H100 cheaper due to higher throughput. I attached the calc in the run blob.

benchbot: uploaded attachments: s3://redwood-bench/1951234567/run-metrics.csv, s3://redwood-bench/1951234567/kernel-profiles.json

tara.s: did you try int8 quant on either? any quality regressions?

marta: ran q4f16 on both for a small eval set: perplexity + ROUGE delta minimal (<1%). tokens/sec up ~15% on A100, ~12% on H100. cost/1M drops by same ratio. quality lookahead okay but we need larger eval to be confident.

jonathan: can you produce a 1-page slide for ops: recommended default for PLG customers and enterprise customers?

marta: yes — I'll push a short doc by EOD. recommendation draft: default hosted = H100 in region parity for latency-sensitive apps; offer A100 pockets for low-util or cost-sensitive steady workloads.

rahul: thanks. also let's add a routing policy that prefers H100 for requests <200ms SLA and A100 for background batch.

marta: noted. will file a routing PR and link the slide.

jonathan: thanks all :thumbsup:
